text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-A tax expert doubts the tax returns of planning minister Terje Roed-Larsen, who has come under fire for buying share options nearly 10 years ago and selling them with a huge profit.
-The army is unhappy that fewer and fewer young men seek a military career.
-The defence authorities want to buy six new transport planes because Norwegian troops are increasingly sent on overseas assignments.
-Poor nine-month results for investment group RGI are not expected to cause problems for Kjell-Inge Roekke's plans to merge his company with Aker.
-Foreign Aid Minister Kari Nordheim-Larsen threatens to halt new aid projects in Namibia because the country's president, Sam Nujoma, plans to buy a new presidential plane and two helicopters.
-Orkla will probably sell half of frozen-food subsidiary Frionor to RGI's Norway Seafoods in return for shares in the company.
-Interest rates rose as the crown weakened.
